title: They didn’t break the Church from the outside.
paragraphs: They didn’t break the Church from the outside.
We helped from within.
Quietly. Respectably. In Sunday clothes.
Here are 7 ways we partner with darkness without even realizing it—

1. We tolerate “small” sin.
Not the scandalous kind. The “manageable” kind. Pride. Gossip. Lust in secret.
We call it weakness. God calls it poison.
“Be holy…” (1 Peter 1:16)

2. We replace repentance with routine.
We show up. Sing loud. Lift hands.
But never surrender.
Church attendance without heart transformation is spiritual theater.

3. We divide over preferences, not truth.
Music style. Leadership style. Personal offense.
The enemy doesn’t need to destroy us—just divide us.
“But if you bite and devour one another…” (Galatians 5:15)

4. We elevate leaders above Christ.
When a pastor falls, our faith collapses.
Why? Because we built on personality, not the Person of Jesus.
Only Christ is unshakable.

5. We stay silent when truth costs us.
We fear losing approval more than losing purity.
So we whisper truth in private… and compromise in public.
That silence? It’s not neutral. It’s surrender.

6. We play with temptation instead of fleeing it.
We scroll longer. Chat deeper. Linger closer.
Then act surprised when we fall.
“Flee youthful lusts…” (2 Timothy 2:22)

7. We forget the Gospel is for us too.
We preach grace to others—but live condemned ourselves.
Or worse—we stop preaching grace at all.
A Church without the Gospel becomes a museum of masks.
But here’s what we miss…
Jesus already saw all this—and still chose the Church.

Not because we’re clean.
But because He makes us clean.

The cross is not just where sinners are forgiven—
It’s where the Church is rebuilt.
Right now.
Right here.

Repentance is not humiliation.
It’s restoration.

Grace is not permission.
It’s power.

So if this pierced something in you—good.
That’s not shame. That’s the Spirit calling you home.
Come back.

Not to religion.
To Jesus.

He doesn’t abandon His Church.
He purifies it.
And He’s not done with you.
Pray through it.
